note: Day 3 of the short U3 (SHULL-CHG-0054). Covers 3.4 electronegativity, 3.6 explaining the trends, 3.7 ion formation; comes after the Periodic Trends Gizmo (radius, IE, metallic character). One deck spans three sections, so each slide sets its own footer code and the file is named at unit level. Charges use ^{...} superscript markup (build_deck.js richText); the minus is U+2212.

fields.headline:
Trends
and Ions
fields.subhead: Electronegativity, why the trends happen, and the ions atoms form.

imageSubjects.section: a row of sealed glass vials holding element samples: a gray metal, yellow sulfur, a red-brown liquid

fields.headline: What the Gizmo Showed You
fields.subhead: Atoms get smaller across a period and bigger down a group. Ionization energy does the opposite.
fields.keyq: Why would a smaller atom hold on to its electrons more tightly?

imageSubjects.concept: a magnet holding steel paper clips, close-up, dark bench

fields.headline: Three Words for Today
fields.subhead: Write these first. The rest of the deck uses all three.
fields.k1_b: How strongly an atom pulls on electrons it shares in a bond.
fields.k2_b: A positive ion. The atom lost electrons.
fields.k3_b: A negative ion. The atom gained electrons.
fields.mustwrite: Electronegativity is an atom's pull on the electrons it shares in a bond.

imageSubjects.aside: a chemistry notebook open to a hand-ruled vocabulary page

fields.headline: Ionization Energy vs. Electronegativity
fields.subhead: They sound alike. One is about losing an electron, the other about pulling on a shared one.
fields.c1_b:
Energy needed to pull one electron off an atom.

Measured in kJ/mol.
fields.c2_b:
Pull on electrons shared with another atom.

No units. Fluorine is highest at 4.0.
fields.mustwrite: Both rise across a period and fall down a group.

imageSubjects.concept: two hands pulling on opposite ends of a rope, cropped tight

fields.headline: Electronegativity Across Period 2
fields.subhead: Down group 17 it falls: F 4.0, Cl 3.2, Br 3.0, I 2.7.
fields.k1_b:
1.0

A metal. It lets go of electrons easily.
fields.k2_b:
2.6

In the middle. It shares electrons.
fields.k3_b:
4.0

The strongest pull of any element.
fields.mustwrite: Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group.

imageSubjects.aside: a sealed glass ampoule of pale yellow gas

fields.headline:
Why the
Trends Happen
fields.subhead: Two ideas explain radius, ionization energy and electronegativity.

imageSubjects.divider: a dark bench with a single glowing hydrogen discharge tube

fields.headline: Two Things Control the Pull
fields.subhead: Every trend today comes from these two.
fields.c1_b:
More protons pull harder on every electron.

Across a period, each element adds one proton.
fields.c2_b:
Inner electrons block part of that pull.

Down a group, each period adds an energy level.
fields.mustwrite: More protons pull harder. More energy levels put electrons farther out.

imageSubjects.concept: concentric ripples on dark water seen from above

fields.headline: One Picture, Three Trends
fields.subhead: Label the arrows on your Gizmo sheet, including the diagonal.
fields.a1_b: Radius shrinks. Ionization energy and EN rise.
fields.a2_b: Radius grows. Ionization energy and EN fall.

fields.headline: Example: Which Atom Is Smaller?
fields.subhead: We do this one together. The reason matters more than the answer.
fields.problem: Which atom is smaller, sodium or chlorine? Explain using nuclear charge.
fields.g1_b:
Both in period 3
Na: 11 protons
Cl: 17 protons
fields.mustwrite: Same period: compare protons. Same group: compare energy levels.

imageSubjects.aside: a small pile of sodium metal under oil in a dish

fields.headline: Sodium vs. Chlorine, Worked
fields.subhead: Name the trend, compare the atoms, then give the reason.
fields.f1_b:
Same period
Same 3 energy levels
Compare protons
fields.work:
Cl has 6 more protons.
Stronger pull, same levels.
Chlorine is smaller.
fields.mustwrite: Across a period, more protons pull the electrons in closer.

fields.headline: Your Turn: Higher Ionization Energy?
fields.subhead: Work it in your notes, then we compare.
fields.problem: Which has the higher ionization energy, magnesium or barium? Explain using energy levels.
fields.g1_b:
Both in group 2
Mg: period 3
Ba: period 6
fields.mustwrite: Name the trend first, then give the reason.

imageSubjects.aside: a strip of magnesium ribbon coiled on a watch glass

fields.headline: Magnesium vs. Barium, Worked
fields.subhead: Check yours against this before we move on.
fields.work:
Mg: 3 levels. Ba: 6 levels.
Mg's outer electron is closer.
Magnesium has the higher IE.
fields.mustwrite: Down a group, outer electrons are farther away and easier to remove.

fields.headline:
Ion
Formation
fields.subhead: Atoms gain or lose electrons until they match the nearest noble gas.

imageSubjects.divider: table salt crystals under a hand lens, macro, dark ground

fields.headline: Metals Lose, Nonmetals Gain
fields.subhead: Each one ends with the electron arrangement of a noble gas.
fields.mustwrite: Metals lose electrons and form cations. Nonmetals gain electrons and form anions.

imageSubjects.aside: a beaker of clear salt water on a white bench

fields.headline: The Rest of the Main Groups
fields.subhead: Group 14 usually shares electrons instead. That is Unit 4.
fields.mustwrite: The charge is the number of electrons lost (+) or gained (−).

imageSubjects.aside: a roll of aluminum foil, edge on, soft light

fields.headline: Ions Are Not the Same Size as Their Atoms
fields.subhead: Circles drawn to scale. Outlined: neutral atom. Filled: its ion.
fields.a1_b: It loses its outer energy level, so it shrinks.
fields.a2_b: Same protons, more electrons repelling, so it grows.
fields.a3_b: Na 186 pm to 102 pm. Cl 99 pm to 181 pm.

fields.headline: Example: Predict the Ion
fields.subhead: Use the group number. Then decide which way the size goes.
fields.problem: Predict the ion formed by calcium and by sulfur. Which ion is larger than its atom?
fields.mustwrite: For main-group elements, the group tells you the charge.

imageSubjects.aside: a lump of yellow sulfur on a watch glass

fields.headline: Calcium and Sulfur, Worked
fields.subhead: Charge first, then size.
fields.f1_b:
Ca loses 2 electrons
S gains 2 electrons
fields.work:
Ca^{2+}: cation, smaller
S^{2−}: anion, larger
S^{2−} is larger than S.
fields.mustwrite: A cation is smaller than its atom. An anion is larger.

fields.headline: Check Yourself
fields.subhead: Two minutes in your notes. Then we go over it.
fields.c1_b:
Lowest to highest:

K, Br, Ca
fields.c2_b:
Write the ion each forms:

Li, O, Al
fields.mustwrite: Write both answers before the next slide.

imageSubjects.concept: a stopwatch on a lab bench

fields.headline: Check Yourself, Answers
fields.subhead: Fix anything you missed in your notes.
fields.c1_b:
K < Ca < Br

All three are in period 4. EN rises left to right.
fields.mustwrite: Metals form positive ions. Nonmetals form negative ions.
